changed_views: A usable recommendation workflow still requires validation beyond a functioning dashboard.
follow_ups: Measure recommendation usefulness, confidence calibration, document accuracy, data controls and retained paid usage.

signals.claim: Sokhal says Moshi connects public and private market data to recommend information relevant to a trader's portfolio.
signals.evidence: An ontology and graph support proactive recommendations alongside queries. The claimed ingestion rate has no defined unit or accuracy benchmark.

signals.claim: Sokhal treats disagreement between trusted sources as information to preserve.
signals.evidence: She describes confidence scores and contextualizing conflicting reports. No calibration results establish whether those scores predict correctness.

signals.claim: Sokhal links internal document models to customer-data controls and available engineering talent.
signals.evidence: She describes extracting uploaded PDFs and avoiding uncontrolled third-party processing. This does not establish on-premises deployment, universal confidentiality or better extraction economics.

summary: Anekha Sokhal describes Moshi's commodity-research system: portfolio-specific recommendations, source disagreement and privately processed documents. The interview supplies product mechanisms, without measured trading performance or adoption.
why_it_matters: Its differentiation depends on useful connections and workflow adoption, beyond ingesting more information. Customer data handling also shapes the architecture.
